text:
Predicates:
Timeless(x) ::: x is timeless.
DesignStyle(x, y) ::: x has design style y.
MassProductDesign(x) ::: x is a mass product design.
Evocative(x) ::: x is evocative.
Dreamy(x) ::: x is dreamy.
DesignBy(x, y) ::: x is a design by y.
Max(x) ::: x is Max.
ZahaHadid(x) ::: x is Zaha Hadid.
KellyWearstler(x) ::: x is Kelly Wearstler.
PublishYear(y, z) ::: y was published in year z.

Premises:
∀x (DesignStyle(zahaHadid, x) → Timeless(x)) ::: All of Zaha Hadid's design styles are timeless.
¬∃x (DesignStyle(y, x) ∧ MassProductDesign(x)) ::: No mass product design is timeless.
DesignStyle(zahaHadid, y) ∨ DesignStyle(kellyWearstler, y) ::: Either Zaha Hadid's design style or Kelly Wearstler's design style.
∀x (DesignStyle(kellyWearstler, x) → Evocative(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles are evocative.
∀x (DesignStyle(kellyWearstler, x) → Dreamy(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles are dreamy.
∀x (DesignBy(max, x) ∧ Timeless(x) → MassProductDesign(x) ∧ Evocative(x)) ::: If a design by Max is timeless, then it is a mass product design and evocative.

Conclusion:
DesignBy(max, y) ∧ (Evocative(y) ∨ Dreamy(y)) ::: A design by Max is either evocative or dreamy.
